supported_claim: For the retained q03 question and exactly these three authored fictional answers, the first tutor trajectories produced content-appropriate feedback and bounded answer-conditioned durable state: scoped support, scoped challenge, and checkpoint-only unresolved reasoning. Each fresh successor used its actual bounded durable readback to continue the saved teaching step while preserving unresolved claims and source-occurrence boundaries. All eighteen retained host requests reproduced exactly in the fake provider, with no model resampling during replay.
scope_and_method_limits: All learner answers are authored synthetic fixtures. No real learner participated; correctness of actual learner assessment, learning benefit, retention and transfer are not measured.

This is one retained first model trajectory per answer and one per distinct actual readback. It demonstrates only this bounded controlled-input contrast, not a reliability rate, population estimate or robust model-level causal effect.
The historical q03 question was supplied. This does not test choosing the question autonomously, unseen-domain transfer, or the diagnostic-question selection policy.
The request explicitly asked for a sensible stopping point and a fresh next session. Closure and checkpoint behavior are task-driven; autonomous detection of a stopping boundary is not established.

Recovery uses a fixed existing-host selection recipe. Successors do not autonomously discover arbitrary context, and failure/denied/missing/over-budget recovery was not part of these six trajectories.

The fake provider uses static version tokens and fixed fixture time. Actual read ordering and exact operation replay do not prove production freshness, true CAS concurrency, provider credential isolation or real deployment fencing.

A bridge call reconstructs the fake provider and opens/closes its own host session. The unrestarted trajectory refers to the consumer run, not a continuously live broker session or an OS-crash recovery test.

Consumers and reviewer are instruction-isolated contexts using the same model family and shared filesystem. This is quality amplification, not independent-provider attestation or a security sandbox. Exact backend build, seed, temperature and complete provider prompt are not exposed.

The final source hash guard was added before prospective freeze after the candidate-2 review and is explicitly disclosed. Sealing/replay helpers are deterministic postprocessing authored after freeze, not preregistered code. The frozen criteria and consumer packets remain unchanged.

The observed C trajectories made no writes. Successor-side repair, justified reinterpretation-event creation and failed-write recovery are therefore not demonstrated; C does not erase or relabel any B outcome.

The support and challenge observations belong to separate counterfactual worlds sharing a fictional source-round identifier. They must not be pooled as repeated independent performances by one learner.
Passing the frozen synthetic task is not a Core #34 blanket pass, deployment, project acceptance, real-state mutation authorization or basis for changing product protocols.
review_boundary: Only review JSON files were authored by the reviewer in the experiment root. No consumer was invoked, output altered, Core source changed, public comment sent, or action outside this synthetic review scope performed.
